I read the structure region by region and assembled the SMILES from the pieces below.

**Left side.** The core is a 7H-pyrrolo[2,3-d]pyrimidine. C2 carries an NH–aryl group and C4 carries an NH–indoline group.
- The indoline is attached through its C7 position, and its nitrogen is N-mesyl (N–S(=O)(=O)CH3).
- The aryl group is a benzene ring with an OMe group and a piperidin-1-yl group on adjacent carbons.

**Middle.** The piperidine carries a piperazin-1-yl group at its 4-position. The other piperazine nitrogen is acylated by C(=O) to azetidine C3. The azetidine nitrogen is attached to the isoindoline-1,3-dione at position 5. The isoindoline nitrogen carries a 2,6-dioxopiperidin-3-yl group.

**Pyrrolopyrimidine SMILES.** I wrote the core as c1(N...)nc(N...)c2cc[nH]c2n1, with C2 as the first atom, N3 next, then C4 bearing the indoline NH. C4 is bonded to C4a, which is bonded to C5, then C6, then N7H, then C7a, and C7a closes onto N1. The ring-closure digits in the final string differ from this fragment because the pieces are joined.

**Phenyl ring.** The NH sits on the ring carbon at the left. Going around the ring, the carbon bearing OMe is adjacent to the carbon bearing the piperidine N, and the NH carbon is meta to the OMe carbon. Ring atoms: c1(NH) – cH – c(OMe) – c(N-piperidine) – cH – cH, closing back to c1. In the drawing, the NH carbon is at the upper left, the CH above it leads to the OMe carbon, and the piperidine carbon is then lower right, so this matches.

**Indoline.** The indoline C7 carries the NH. C7 is bonded to C7a, which bears the N, so the NH-bearing carbon is adjacent to the N-bearing carbon. SMILES: Nc1cccc2CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)c12.

**Full SMILES.**
COc1cc(Nc2nc(Nc3cccc4CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)c34)c5cc[nH]c5n2)ccc1N6CCC(CC6)N7CCN(CC7)C(=O)C8CN(C8)c9ccc%10C(=O)N(C(=O)%10c9)C%11CCC(=O)NC%11=O

**Isoindoline ring check.** The azetidine is attached at c9, which sits on the benzene ring. The ring is c9 c c c%10 … c%10 c9 and the closure is correct. Benzene atoms are c9 (azetidine-bearing), c, c, c%10 (carries C(=O)), c%10' (carries the other C=O), and c (the CH between c%10' and c9). I wrote c9ccc%10C(=O)N(...)C(=O)%10c9, which makes the second carbonyl carbon close to the ring atom %10. That is wrong, because %10 closes on the aromatic atom, so I need a correct form.

Corrected fragment: c9ccc%10c(c9)C(=O)N(C%11CCC(=O)NC%11=O)C%10=O

Here c%10 is the carbon bearing the C(=O) that closes at the end, and the next atom c(c9) bears the other C(=O). This matches the drawing.

SMILES: COc1cc(Nc2nc(Nc3cccc4CCN(S(C)(=O)=O)c34)c5cc[nH]c5n2)ccc1N6CCC(CC6)N7CCN(CC7)C(=O)C8CN(C8)c9ccc%10c(c9)C(=O)N(C%11CCC(=O)NC%11=O)C%10=O
